stem.text: The diagram shows the distribution of molecular energies in a sample of gas at a temperature $T_1$. The activation energy for an uncatalysed reaction of this gas, $E_{\text{a(uncat)}}$, is shown.

stem.alt: Graph of proportion of molecules with a given energy against molecular energy E, with a single curve peaking at T1, and a dashed line marking Ea(uncat) on the high-energy tail.

stem.text: Which diagram correctly shows the new distribution and new activation energy, $E_{\text{a(cat)}}$, when the temperature is increased to $T_2$, and a catalyst is used that increases the rate of the reaction?

A.alt: Solid T1 and dashed T2 curves, with T2 peaking to the left of T1. The Ea(uncat) dashed line is left of the Ea(cat) dashed line.

B.alt: Solid T1 and dashed T2 curves, with T2 peaking to the left of T1. The Ea(cat) dashed line is left of the Ea(uncat) dashed line.

C.alt: Solid T1 and dashed T2 curves, with T2 peaking to the right of T1. The Ea(cat) dashed line is left of the Ea(uncat) dashed line.

D.alt: Solid T1 and dashed T2 curves, with T2 peaking to the right of T1. The Ea(cat) dashed line is right of the Ea(uncat) dashed line.
